Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. Per our conversation I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan that lays out the evaluation checkpoints and a suggested close runway so your team can pick the hosting mode (Hosted, Dedicated, or Private). High-level items in the MAP:

- Week 1: security questionnaire & SOC2 snapshot review (we provided a lightweight artifact)
- Week 2–3: performance evaluation (latency/throughput) against sample traffic using Hosted + Dedicated baseline
- Week 4: ops & compliance sign-off; if Private is chosen we add an infra readiness window

Decision criteria we recommend you prioritize: data residency, max P95 latency, peak qps, and procurement timeline. If you lean Private we should budget ~6–8 weeks for VPC/on-prem packaging and validation; Dedicated is typically 2–3 weeks for capacity reservation and smoke tests; Hosted can be validated in your PoC window (~5 business days) but has different SLAs.

I've attached: helix_MAP_v2.pdf (MAP with milestones) and a SOC2 snapshot for your compliance team. Can you confirm who from your side will own procurement and security for the MAP? Once we have that, we can lock the calendar and target a final decision date.

Proposed close target: 2026-04-18 (exec review on 2026-04-20) — flexible if you need more runway.

Next steps:
- You: confirm procurement + security owners
- Us: schedule perf baseline (we can run Hosted + Dedicated tests) and provide Dedicated sizing guidance

Thanks —

Elena —

Great questions. Short answers up front: Private timeline (6–8 weeks) does include network review and KMS/HSM integration if you opt for our on-prem bundle and agree to the initial network changes during week 1–2. If you require additional site audits or air-gapped validation we should treat that as a separate line item and plan ~+2 weeks.

Dedicated lead time: to guarantee a steady baseline with reserved capacity we generally require a 10 business day lead to provision and validate nodes, with an option to reserve burst capacity. If you need full production SLA on Dedicated, plan for a 2–3 week ramp (provisioning + canary + load validation). For your Apr 26 window, Dedicated is feasible only if we confirm sizing and sign the reservation by Apr 14.

Suggested tweak to the MAP: add a "procurement hold" milestone on Apr 14 as the gating item for Dedicated. If procurement takes longer, fallback plan is Hosted for the PoC and Dedicated for go-live.

I'll update the MAP PDF to include explicit gating milestones and a short table showing tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs isolation). New version attached.

Adding a quick technical note from the infra side — Elena / Elisa:

- Dedicated sizing: if your peak is ~150 qps with 1.5k token average responses, recommended starting pool = 4 x A100-equivalent nodes with continuous batching enabled. That gives headroom for burst and allows us to keep P95 < 350ms in our tests.
- Autoscale for Dedicated: warm-up takes ~3–5 minutes per added node under our current autoscaler; for strict latency SLOs we recommend pre-warmed burst capacity during expected traffic spikes.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): we can run the same binaries but need your VPN termination + static egress rules. KMS integration is via standard PKCS11/HSM paths — our security engineer can vendor-validate in week 1.

If you want, we can run a short perf baseline on Hosted first (48–72 hours) to collect real metrics and then run Dedicated tests with identical request traces. That will give a clean apples-to-apples comparison for your MAP decision.

Karthik
